thread.title: Apple misses on iPhone sales in first months of iPhone 8, iPhone X availability (AAPL)

title: Apple misses on iPhone sales in first months of iPhone 8, iPhone X availability (AAPL)
text: Apple loses its big bet on the future of iPhone as holiday sales disappoint (AAPL) Kif Leswing More Getty Apple delivered record revenue and profit in its first quarter earnings on Thursday, but sales of the iPhone, the company's most important product, declined year-over-year. The company also provided a forecast for next quarter that was significantly lower than Wall Street was expecting. Apple shares dropped over 1% lower in after-hours trading on Thursday. However, the shortfall in iPhone sales were made up by a significantly higher average iPhone price — $796, over $100 more than the average iPhone price last holiday season. That sharp increase in average iPhone prices is likely due to the iPhone X, Apple's highest-end phone, with a starting price of $999. Still, the iPhone maker delivered a big quarter. Here are the key numbers: Revenue : $88.3 billion, up 12.6% year-over-year, versus expectations of $87.1 billion Earnings per share (GAAP) : $3.89, up 15.7% year over year, versus expectations of $3.83 Gross margin: 38.4%, flat year-over-year, verus expectations of 38.4% iPhone sales : 77.3 million units, down 0.9% year-over-year, versus expectations of 80.2 million iPhone average selling price : $796, up 15% year-over-year, versus expectations of 767. iPad sales: 13.1 million, flat year-over-year Mac sales: 5.1 million, flat year-over-year Q2 guidance: Between $60 billion and $62 billion, versus expectations of $67.1 billion Here's a chart with the key sales figures: Apple Q1 2018
